title: cost-pulse-regulator-and-quant-pruner
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Large fleets show sustained token cost drift from a small fraction of tenants whose coldstart and microburst patterns defeat current batching and prefill defaults. This PR introduces two cooperating features: Cost Pulse Regulator (a tenant-level warmup and transient-budget controller) and Quant Pruner (a conservative quantization profile shrinker that trims non-impactful low-importance weights for warm tenants). The goal is to reduce unit cost on high-variance traffic while preserving tail latency and quality SLOs.

Design summary: The Cost Pulse Regulator attaches to the request routing layer and maintains a short-lived per-tenant pulse budget. It smooths bursts by: 1) coordinating short prefills for tenants flagged as burst-prone, 2) dynamically lowering preferred batch target for cold windows, and 3) gating optimistic cache reuse when latency headroom is tight. The Quant Pruner runs as a background job in the model profile pipeline: it takes an existing quant profile, evaluates a low-cost sensitivity scan on a sampled prompt set, and applies small, conservative pruning steps (per-channel thresholds) that have measured <0.5% BLEU-like quality drift on the sampled eval.

Implementation notes: - New package: pkg/econ/pulse_regulator.go implements the regulator state machine and exposes a lean API used by the router. - New package: pkg/quant/pruner.go implements the prune-and-simulate loop, with dry-run and apply modes. - API: costctl suggest now includes --pulse and --prune flags; Console shows a new CostPulse heatmap and a quant-prune preview. - Telemetry: added econ.pulse.{allocated,consumed,throttled}, quant.prune.{candidate_count,applied_count,estimated_risk}. - Safety: all prune actions are staged as suggested changes and require tenant opt-in for Private Dedicated customers; Hosted gets an opt-out list.

Checklist: - [x] Core regulator state machine and API wired to router. - [x] Quant pruner prototype with sensitivity scan. - [x] E2E smoke that simulates tenant microbursts and verifies no >5% latency tail regressions. - [x] Telemetry dashboards + alert thresholds added. - [x] Documentation and console UI stub.

Testing: Unit tests for state transitions and prune heuristics added. E2E synthetic run against prefiller with a 10k request trace shows ~12-18% cost reduction on bursty tenants and median tail latency increase <2%. CI included simulated load tests.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to canary tenants in staging (2/25), 2) run 48h cost/quality canary with traffic shadowing, 3) enable auto-suggest for high-variance tenants (opt-in) while keeping apply locked. Full rollout contingent on telemetry signal.

Rollback: regulator runs behind a feature flag; pruner applies changes as candidate diffs until explicitly accepted. Remove flag or revoke tenant opt-in to revert impact.

review_comments: Lars Becker: Please add a metric for 'pulse_rejected' so we can track how often we deny a prefill. Also call out expected memory overhead per tenant.
Aisha Kapoor: Added pulse_rejected metric; regulator stores only 128B of state per tenant in memory on average (updated docs).
Maya Chen: Quant pruning looks promising — include an explicit guard to prevent pruning when eval diversity score is below threshold; otherwise we risk overfitting to small samples.
Aisha Kapoor: Implemented diversity guard and added integration test to exercise low-diversity failure mode; documented opt-in requirement for production apply.
Diego Alvarez: CI flaky on synthetic e2e — tracked to timing in router; suggested increasing test timeouts and backing off non-deterministic sleep. Fixed and re-ran.
Lars Becker: approved after telemetry and safety comments addressed.
ci_log_summary: All checks passed on latest run: unit, lint, e2e-synthetic, integration; one flaky test fixed during review, re-ran. Coverage change: +0.6%
release_notes: Introduced Cost Pulse Regulator to smooth tenant microbursts and Quant Pruner to suggest conservative quant-profile trims. Early canary saw cost reductions for bursty tenants; features are gated behind flags and require tenant opt-in for apply. No breaking changes to public API.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag 'econ.pulse.enabled' in staging for canary tenants. Watch econ.pulse.throttled and quant.prune.estimated_risk dashboards. Set alert: >2% SLA tail regression for 1h to trigger automatic rollback.
